articles.summary: Tim’s view Climate diplomacy is deeply broken. The latest dire United Nations projection, published on Wednesday, stressed that the ambitions to limit global warming adopted a decade ago in Paris are all but out of reach , absent an urgent economic and political pivot that appears nowhere on the horizon. Blowing past 1.5℃ of warming is inevitable, and even the most far-fetched techniques possible to claw temperatures back down probably won’t return it to that level in the future. Warming is instead on track to reach 2.8℃ this century, the report said. articles.author: Prashant Rao
articles.summary: French authorities readied a heavy security presence ahead of planned weekend protests, aiming to head off instability that has called into question the country’s long-term economic prospects. Demonstrations last week erupted into violence , including mass looting and cars being set alight, resulting in more than 2,000 arrests. The unrest has huge domestic and international implications: Analysts argue the violence bolsters the case made by the far-right — the favorite in 2027 elections — that the current leadership is ineffective, while foreign investors, who hold the majority of France’s mammoth government debt, may grow skeptical that Paris can get to grips with its budget. “ A ‘perfect storm’ appears to be forming over the French economy ,” a Le Monde columnist warned. — Prashant Rao
